title: How many executions will be carried out in the US in 2026?
resolution_criteria: This question resolves as the total number of people in the United States who were executed by state and federal governmental authorities in 2026, according to the [Death Penalty Information Center](https://deathpenaltyinfo.org/facts-and-research/data/executions) (DPIC).
fine_print: This question may also resolve according to [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions). Please note that US military executions count even if they are not included in the DPIC total.

comments.author: DaiLothbrook
exmateriae
comments.text:
On October 8, DPIC listed [30 prisoners executed](https://deathpenaltyinfo.org/executions/2026) in 6 states in 2026, with Florida accounting for 16 of the 30. Nine executions are [still scheduled](https://deathpenaltyinfo.org/executions/upcoming-executions) by EOY.

### Tennessee

To my understanding, Tennessee is out for 2026 because of the Sept 30 failed execution oh Christa Pike, capital punishment has been [halted until next year](https://philstarlife.com/news-and-views/614615-christa-pike-final-words-before-her-failed-execution) after that. That should also cancel Gary Sutton's Dec 3 date, [which DPIC still showed as active](https://deathpenaltyinfo.org/executions/upcoming-executions/outcomes-of-warrants/outcomes-of-death-warrants-in-2026) before the halt.

This might be a weird edge case that I'll ask Claude to include in the Monte Carlo: she was [still unconscious on a ventilator](https://www.boldsky.com/insync/who-is-christa-pike-how-did-the-us-death-row-inmate-survive-two-lethal-injection-doses-173153.html). If she dies before EOY, would DPIC call that an execution? Precedent seems to go towards no: Broom and Hamm survived their failed attempts and were never counted. \~4–5% this adds +1.

### Florida

Florida withdrew a warrant for the first time: DeSantis canceled William Lee Thompson's execution scheduled for Oct. 13, pending a psychiatric evaluation but afaict, that still seems [likely to happen this year](https://deathpenaltyinfo.org/executions/upcoming-executions/outcomes-of-warrants/outcomes-of-death-warrants-in-2026)? DeSantis has weird incentives in that he broke the record of executions last year and could one up it this year.

Guardado (Nov 5) would be #19 and tie the 2025 record. The [warrant coverage](https://cbs12.com/news/local/desantis-signs-death-warrant-for-record-20th-execution-of-year-jesse-guardado-2024-murder-walton-county-woman-) says he would have been #20 to break the record but that was still counting Thompson. I'm not exactly sure what the probabilities are on this one but the incentives are there. This is DeSantis last term and the record is really close and would help him strengthen the image he wants to have. 

Last year Florida executed [four people](https://www.mysuncoast.com/2025/12/19/florida-executes-its-19th-inmate-2025) between November 6 and December 31. Warrants come 4–5 weeks ahead: Walls’s Dec 18 date was [signed Nov 18](https://www.wsls.com/news/national/2025/11/19/florida-sets-execution-date-for-man-who-fatally-shot-man-and-woman-during-home-invasion-robbery/). There's still plenty time.

### **Hasan (Military)**

**From an outsider POV, this seems like a pretty weird case.** Trump approved on October 2the first military execution since 1961, the Army [set the date on Oct 6](https://taskandpurpose.com/news/nidal-hasan-execution/) and the Pentagon wants it [livestreamed](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cmy0r96xygx6o). He could still file for habeas which would likely bring the execution to [next year](https://www.news4jax.com/news/politics/2026/10/09/legal-path-seems-narrow-to-challenge-livestream-of-fort-hood-shooters-execution-experts-say/), at least in part because he [didn’t have a lawyer](https://federalnewsnetwork.com/defense-news/2026/10/pentagon-says-the-firing-squad-execution-of-fort-hood-shooter-nidal-malik-hasan-will-be-livestreamed-in-december/) at the time of notification so he might simply not have been aware? New counsel with less than two months would kill this but from what I've read, his trial behavior indicated he likely won't. Also, the last presidential approval, Ronald Gray’s in 2008, [ended in a stay](https://www.army.mil/article/14882/scheduled_execution_of_pvt_ronald_a_gray_stayed).

### **Other states**

Humphreys in Georgia [got a stay](https://www.fox5atlanta.com/news/judge-stays-execution-convicted-murder-stacey-humphreys) from a county judge so that will wait for next year. (is it possible for something really quick to happen here?)

Surprisingly, there's a legislation that stops Texas from having other executions this year? Art. 43.141 [requires 91 days](https://texas.public.law/statutes/tex._code_of_crim._proc._article_43.141) between the order and the execution date.

Oklahoma may have one with Pavatt [on November 12](https://www.kgou.org/criminal-justice/2026-08-28/execution-date-set-for-oklahoma-county-killer) but the governor has granted clemency before, eg [Tremane Wood](https://deathpenaltyinfo.org/stories/oklahoma-governor-kevin-stitt-grants-clemency-to-tremane-wood) a year ago.

In Louisiana, the 5th Circuit [reversed Todd Wessinger's habeas relief](https://www.wafb.com/2026/08/18/execution-death-row-inmate-todd-wessinger-will-move-forward-appeals-court-rules/) on August 18. He [sued over nitrogen](https://content.wbrz.com/news/a-death-row-inmate-convicted-of-two-1995-murders-is-suing-to-block-his-nitrogen-gas-execution) and there’s no date yet but the state has gone from [warrant to execution](https://lailluminator.com/2025/02/11/louisiana-execution/) in \~5 weeks with Hoffman last year, so December is still possible.

From there, I asked Claude for an estimation of each person's probability of execution, didn't adjust much on that: (and gave me a few additional facts)

| Date   | Inmate           | Key fact                                                                                                                                                                             | P(executed) |
| ------ | ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------- |
| Oct 13 | Robertson (FL)   | Volunteer, pleaded guilty and waived all appeals                                                                                                                                     | 96%         |
| Oct 20 | Reaves (FL)      | Lost in circuit court, appeal pending at the Florida Supreme Court                                                                                                                   | 90%         |
| Nov 5  | Guardado (FL)    | Routine Florida warrant                                                                                                                                                              | 93%         |
| Nov 5  | Weisheit (IN)    | No drugs had been acquired for the Nov. 5 execution, clemency hearings in October                                                                                                    | 65%         |
| Nov 5  | Taylor (AL)      | Warrant obtained for nitrogen, then switched to lethal injection after a federal court ruled the nitrogen protocol unconstitutional. Lee went ahead on Sept 18 after the same switch | 82%         |
| Nov 12 | Rubio (TX)       | Pending competency-to-be-executed claim, previously diagnosed with schizophrenia                                                                                                     | 62%         |
| Nov 12 | Pavatt (OK)      | Innocence-based clemency bid, hearing Oct. 14                                                                                                                                        | 82%         |
| Nov 19 | Dennes (TX)      | No notable live litigation found                                                                                                                                                     | 85%         |
| Dec 3  | Hasan (Military) | See above                                                                                                                                                                            | 35%         |

### **M**onte Carlo, 300k runs:

5% chance of another failure or a SCOTUS move. (might be high? would rather err on uncertainty for now)

New Florida dates: 0–5, mean \~2.5, each \~93% to go through. Other states: a small Poisson(0.3) for AL, AZ, GA, LA, MS.

Most of the uncertainty is whether the scheduled failures cancel out the new Florida dates, which is why 39 and 40 are pretty uncertain.

| Scenario                            | \<39 | 39 | 40 | 41 | >41 | IQR   |
| ----------------------------------- | ---- | -- | -- | -- | --- | ----- |
| FL slow, Hasan excluded             | 53   | 22 | 16 | 7  | 2   | 37–39 |
| FL base, Hasan excluded             | 36   | 23 | 21 | 13 | 7   | 38–40 |
| FL base, Hasan counted (P\=.35)     | 30   | 21 | 22 | 16 | 11  | 38–41 |
| FL repeats 2025 pace, Hasan counted | 21   | 17 | 22 | 20 | 20  | 39–41 |



If every date holds and nothing gets added, that's 39. I expect the schedule to lose 1 to 3 dates and Florida to add 2 to 4. Hasan’s firing squad is the other big lever, and per the fine print it counts even if DPIC leaves it out.

Here were the results after the Monte Carlo, which I won't be exactly following but I'm not far away: \<39: 26% · 39: 19% · 40: 22% · 41: 18% · >41: 15%. Median 39–40, IQR 38–41.
